reason: Premises 1–4 are directly supported by the cited UHPS study (E2, E3, E4), which reports full density, 0.7 µm grains, 1.7×10^15 m^-2 dislocations, 46% hardness and 69% toughness increases, and excellent oxidation resistance. The 250 °C oxidation threshold increase is an overstatement not explicitly quantified in the cited evidence. Premise 5 on liquid metal corrosion resistance is not supported by any cited passage, which only mentions oxidation resistance.
premises: UHPS at 15 GPa and 1450 °C fully densifies ZrB2 and refines grains to ~0.7 µm
UHPS increases dislocation density by ~3 orders of magnitude relative to SPS
UHPS simultaneously increases hardness by ~46% and fracture toughness by ~69%
UHPS raises the oxidation threshold temperature by ~250 °C
Refined, defect-minimized microstructure reduces corrosion in liquid plating baths
